method: keywords-explorer-matching-terms, match_mode=phrase, bare noun (not the English 'in' phrasing), volume floor set and limit far above the expected row count so the returned row count is a TRUE tail depth and not a truncated sample.
why_bare_noun: The first probe used 'waterfalls in' / 'wasserfaelle in' / 'cascate in'. That is an English preposition pattern. German parent topics came back as 'wasserfaelle kroatien' and Italian as 'cascate toscana', noun plus place with no preposition, so the prepositional probe undercounted both languages. Same class of error as the French best-time phrasing, caught the same way, by reading parent_topic.

probes.shape: AGGREGATION. Place axis is admin1 (38 US states), country (iceland, costa rica, brazil, croatia, japan, jamaica, zimbabwe, ireland, scotland, australia, canada, mexico, bali, philippines, turkey, dominican republic, argentina, puerto rico), island (oahu, kauai, maui), national park (yosemite, yellowstone, shenandoah), and a minority of cities (portland, seattle, atlanta, austin, san diego, columbus, ithaca, honolulu, asheville, greenville, colorado springs, gatlinburg). NOT every city.
probes.parent_topic_collapse: 'waterfalls in tennessee', 'best waterfalls in tennessee' and 'waterfalls in tn' all collapse to one parent. One page per (place, feature_type) absorbs 2 to 4 phrasings.
probes.serp: local_pack on most, ai_overview on roughly half. Organic positions persist alongside both.

probes.shape: NAMED ENTITY DOMINANT. Individual named falls, not aggregations.
probes.note: Singular 'wasserfall' was NOT sampled by this probe, so the true per-entity tail is larger than 130.

probes.shape: NAMED ENTITY DOMINANT, and far denser than German.
probes.note: Singular 'cascata' was NOT sampled, so the true per-entity tail is larger than 332. The parent topic of the biggest row is 'cascata delle marmore', singular.

probes.shape: NAMED ENTITY DOMINANT at a volume floor of 800, which is a very high floor. The tail below 800 was not sampled and is certainly much larger.
probes.collision_share: Roughly 38 of 257 rows, about 15 percent of rows but a much larger share of volume, are bunk beds, towns named Castello, films, toys and local businesses. This is why the named entity gate is mandatory and why an entity page must be admitted by matching a real entity name, never by matching a keyword pattern.

conclusion.refutes: My earlier position that the OSM outdoor layer is uniformly too thin for own pages and supports only aggregations. That was measured on English prepositional phrasing, which samples the aggregation intent and cannot see the named entity tail at all.
conclusion.holds: Brief B item 10 still holds for peaks. 384,962 peaks at 0.84 facts per entity is the case the brief names, and nothing here contradicts it.
conclusion.correct_model: BOTH layers are real and they are different families. A named outdoor entity with measured demand is class A. A place by feature type aggregation is a separate family with its own measured demand. They do not cannibalise: the German tail carries 'triberger wasserfaelle' AND 'wasserfaelle schwarzwald' as distinct parents.
conclusion.method_for_admission: Intersect the measured tail with real entity names in the store. A matched name is a measured class A entity. An unmatched keyword is noise and is rejected. This is a measurement, not an extrapolation, and it is the only method that scales without querying Ahrefs per page.
